overall: The AG declined to review two allegations (untimely notice challenge for the October 7, 2021 executive session, and a football-incident discussion already addressed in OML 2022-39) and found no Open Meeting Law violation on the remaining allegations, including the April 14, 2022 executive session, the email and text communications, and the notice's warrant item. No order issued; the AG only encouraged more specific warrant descriptions.

allegations.summary: Alleged the committee convened in executive session on October 7, 2021 without listing that session as a topic on the notice.
allegations.key_passage: Because the complaint was not filed with the Committee until May 12, 2022, seven months later, we find that the complaint is untimely with respect to this allegation and decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Alleged the committee failed to discuss whether to investigate an incident at a September 17, 2021 football game.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require a public body to discuss any topic.

allegations.summary: Alleged the committee improperly met in executive session on April 14, 2022 under Purpose 1 to discuss a complaint against the chair.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it discussed the complainant’s letter in executive session.

allegations.summary: Alleged deliberation outside a posted meeting via emails among committee members and the superintendent about investigating the football incident.
allegations.key_passage: Further, even though certain of the emails from Committee members contained his or her opinion on the investigation, a matter within the jurisdiction of the Committee, those opinions were shared only with the Superintendent or with a subquorum of the Committee and therefore did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Alleged the chair deliberated with committee members outside a posted meeting via texts and emails about the complainant's March 2022 letter.
allegations.key_passage: because the communications were only between two members of the Committee, a subquorum, and did not otherwise reach a quorum of the Committee, we find that such communications do not constitute deliberation and therefore the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Alleged a March 28, 2022 email from the chair to all members relayed a conversation about responding to the complaint, constituting improper deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, this email was exempt from the definition of deliberation under the law.

allegations.summary: Alleged the chair deliberated about the complainant's letter with residents before the April 14, 2022 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Here, because any communications regarding the March letter were between Ms. Linares and residents, all of whom are not members of the Committee, and because the communications did not otherwise reach a quorum of the Committee, such communications do not constitute deliberation.

allegations.summary: Alleged the April 14, 2022 meeting notice lacked sufficient detail, specifically the consent agenda item accepting two warrants.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that this consent agenda topic did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
